review_locator: PMCID:PMC3389612, Receptor complexes for each of the Class 3 Semaphorins; PMID:29642487, Semaphorin 3C and Its Receptors in Cancer and Cancer Stem-Like Cells
primary_title: Functional loss of semaphorin 3C and/or semaphorin 3D and their epistatic interaction with ret are critical to Hirschsprung disease liability
decision_basis: The reviews identify class-3 semaphorin receptor complexes containing neuropilins; the cited primary study directly measures AP-SEMA3C binding to Nrp1-expressing cells.
limitations_preserved: NRP1 is a ligand-binding co-receptor rather than a standalone signaling receptor; preserve secreted SEMA3C processing and plexin-complex context; no SCI transfer or autonomous NRP1 relay.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3389612, Receptor complexes for each of the Class 3 Semaphorins; PMID:29642487, Semaphorin 3C and Its Receptors in Cancer and Cancer Stem-Like Cells
primary_title: Semaphorin-3C signals through Neuropilin-1 and PlexinD1 receptors to inhibit pathological angiogenesis
decision_basis: The reviews describe semaphorin signaling through neuropilin-plexin complexes; the cited primary study identifies Sema3C signaling through NRP1 and PlexinD1 in endothelial cells and pathological angiogenesis models.
limitations_preserved: Preserve NRP1/PlexinD1 holoreceptor topology, secreted SEMA3C processing, endothelial/retinal context, and inhibitory angiogenesis function; do not treat SEMA3C as a direct autonomous PlexinD1 ligand or infer SCI relevance.

review_locator: PMID:35636929, Mertk: An emerging target in cancer biology and immuno-oncology; PMCID:PMC3061224, TAM receptors and the clearance of apoptotic cells
primary_title: Auto-oxidation and oligomerization of protein S on the apoptotic cell surface is required for Mer tyrosine kinase-mediated phagocytosis of apoptotic cells
decision_basis: The reviews identify Protein S/PROS1 as a TAM ligand requiring phosphatidylserine context; the cited primary study shows oxidized/oligomerized Protein S preferentially binds and activates human MerTK and drives macrophage efferocytosis.
limitations_preserved: Preserve oxidized/oligomerized Protein S and phosphatidylserine-scaffold dependence; MerTK is a TAM kinase but direct free-ligand equivalence and SCI receiver weighting are not inferred.

review_locator: PMID:24186067, Biology of the TAM receptors; PMID:35636929, Mertk: An emerging target in cancer biology and immuno-oncology
primary_title: Tumour-Secreted Protein S (ProS1) Activates a Tyro3-Erk Signalling Axis and Protects Cancer Cells from Apoptosis
decision_basis: The reviews identify Protein S/PROS1 as a TAM ligand; the cited primary study shows tumor-secreted ProS1 rapidly stimulates Tyro3 and Erk phosphorylation and protects human cancer cells from apoptosis.
limitations_preserved: Cellular cancer context and receptor-family selectivity are bounded; the source establishes activation/ERK association rather than purified binary affinity, and no SCI or universal TAM coupling is inferred.
